transcript:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Ava from Redwood, this is Liam our solutions engineer. Welcome.
[00:07] Dr. Priya Kapoor: Hi thanks, Priya here, CISO at Starlight. We appreciate your time.
[00:12] Ethan Moore: Ethan here, head of platform, I might jump in on infra questions.
[00:16] Ava Martinez: Great, agenda is quick discovery — understand your compliance needs, constraints, and what success looks like. Then we can map Hosted/Dedicated/Private options.
[00:25] Liam Chen: Quick note, I'll probably ask about example traffic, token volumes, and what data types you expect to send to inference.
[00:31] Dr. Priya Kapoor: Sure. High level: we're a regional healthcare provider, moving to embed clinical triage and notes summarization. We'll definitely be sending PHI in prompts, and some EU patient data for cross-border clinics. Main must-haves: full HIPAA compliance, ability to restrict data residency to US-only for some workloads, and strong audit trails that we can export for audits.
[00:51] Sofia Ruiz: From legal, we need clarity on log retention, whether transcripts (raw prompts/responses) are stored, and rights for data deletion for DSARs. Also encryption and BYOK for keys.
[01:05] Ava Martinez: Absolutely. To clarify terminology: Hosted means Redwood-hosted multi-tenant API; Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with customer isolation; Private is VPC/private control plane or on-prem where control plane can be customer-managed. Liam, want to add?
[01:20] Liam Chen: Yeah and from a controls perspective, Hosted can be made HIPAA-safe through contractual controls and restricted logging, but some customers prefer Dedicated or Private because they want no chance data touches shared artifacts, or they want their own KMS.
[01:33] Marcus Bell: When you say "restricted logging" can you be specific — do hosted logs ever contain raw prompt text? We can't have PHI in third-party logs.
[01:41] Liam Chen: Good question. For HIPAA workloads we have a HIPAA offering that limits retention; by default we log metadata for observability. For PHI we can enable redaction and opt-out of storing full transcripts in the hosted offering, but some customers still prefer Dedicated/Private for BYOK and to ensure auditability under their own retention policies.
[02:01] Dr. Priya Kapoor: And what about EU data? GDPR requires that data stays within EU if subject to residency requirements—do you offer EU-only regions for hosted?
[02:09] Ava Martinez: Yes, our hosted API has region routing and we have EU regions — but for stricter residency we recommend Private (VPC or on-prem) or Dedicated pools that are physically in the EU. We also support data processing addenda and standard contractual clauses.
[02:25] Sofia Ruiz: We need to see the DPA and SCCs. Also, is there an easy way to delete all patient data on request? DSARs are a regulatory must.
[02:34] Liam Chen: We provide data deletion endpoints and we can run a full purge for a specific customer or dataset. In Dedicated/Private, you can control retention more directly. In Hosted, we can set retention windows and purge on request — will surface exact SLA in docs.
[02:49] Ethan Moore: For private deployments, what does network isolation look like? We run in AWS and want a VPC peering or private link, no public internet egress for model traffic.
[02:58] Liam Chen: Private supports VPC-only access and private control plane; on-prem is possible for air-gapped setups. We can do VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, or deploy a customer-managed control plane.
[03:10] Marcus Bell: KMS: do you support BYOK with HSM backed keys? We cannot have provider-controlled keys for some PHI workloads.
[03:17] Ava Martinez: Yes, BYOK with HSM/KMS integration is available in Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we offer customer-managed keys on some tiers but the strictest BYOK (HSM) is only available with Private/on-prem or Dedicated with an enterprise contract.
[03:31] Dr. Priya Kapoor: Audit logs — we need immutable logs for access to PHI, and the ability to export to our SIEM. How granular are the logs?
[03:40] Liam Chen: Logs include request/response metadata, caller identity, model version, latency, and optionally full transcripts. For PHI you can disable transcript storage and only keep hashed or redacted pointers. We can forward logs to your SIEM via secure delivery (S3 with SSE-KMS or a direct syslog integration), and retention policies are configurable in Dedicated/Private.
[03:59] Sofia Ruiz: What about e-discovery and legal holds? If there's litigation, we might need to preserve certain records. Who's the custodian?
[04:06] Ava Martinez: In Hosted we'll preserve per contract; in Dedicated/Private you control custody. We can apply legal hold exports on request and provide audit exports. We'll include a section in the DPA around legal hold procedures.
[04:18] Ethan Moore: Performance-wise, we need sub-second latency on triage prompts for chat, and batch summarization overnight. Does Dedicated guarantee latency targets?
[04:27] Liam Chen: Dedicated offers reserved capacity and SLA-backed throughput/latency targets. We can size GPU pools based on your qps/latency requirements; Optimize features like KV caching and batching help with cost/latency tradeoffs.
[04:39] Dr. Priya Kapoor: Regulatory evidence — SOC 2 reports, penetration test results, and HIPAA BAAs. Can you provide those?
[04:45] Ava Martinez: Yes, we'll share SOC 2 Type II, recent pen-test summary, and we have a HIPAA BAA template. I'll attach those after the call (see next steps).
[04:53] Marcus Bell: One risk: logs sometimes accidentally include PII due to prompt templates. Do you support automatic PII detection/redaction at ingestion?
[04:59] Liam Chen: We have a redaction pipeline that can mask or hash PII at ingestion, plus client-side redaction libraries and consistent hashing to allow analytics without exposing raw text. We'll include examples in the security guide.
[05:13] Sofia Ruiz: On the legal side, we need to ensure processors/sub-processors list and subprocessor notifications.
[05:18] Ava Martinez: We'll include our subprocessor list and notification cadence in the DPA.
[05:22] Ethan Moore: Timeline and procurement — we have a pilot board in two weeks and an exec review in 6 weeks. We need costs and a pilot plan to present.
[05:30] Ava Martinez: Understood. Pilot approach: start with Hosted in US region but with HIPAA config (no transcript retention) for low-friction test, and run a parallel Dedicated trial for throughput and BYOK validation. Liam can propose sizing and a benchmark.
[05:42] Liam Chen: Proposed benchmark: small set of representative prompts (triage, notes summarization), measure latency p50/p95, and validate redaction and key flows. We'll run it on a Dedicated pool and document config.
[05:54] Dr. Priya Kapoor: Are there limits to certs or audits we can request? For example, can you provide SOC 2 artifact extracts to our auditors under NDA?
[06:01] Ava Martinez: Yes we can provide SOC2 artifacts under NDA, and sign an auditor access agreement.
[06:08] Marcus Bell: Cost question: what's the delta between Hosted HIPAA-configured and Dedicated? Ballpark.
[06:14] Ava Martinez: Ballpark — Hosted HIPAA with restricted retention is lowest cost; Dedicated adds reserve capacity and isolation, typically 2-3x depending on GPU sizing and committed usage; Private/on-prem includes additional infra and ops costs and is highest. We'll send detailed pricing ranges.
[06:28] Sofia Ruiz: One more, DSAR handling: if a patient requests deletion, how do we assure their data is purged if it's been used to generate embeddings or model outputs?
[06:37] Liam Chen: Embeddings can be treated as derived data; we can delete vectors associated with a subject's identifier and re-run relevant indexes. We'll document typical reindex workflows and timelines. For model outputs, since LLMs are not persistent models updated with your data, there's no model retraining on customer requests unless you explicitly fine-tune with customer data.
[06:59] Dr. Priya Kapoor: Good.
[07:01] Ava Martinez: Ok recap — action items: we'll send SOC2/BAA/HIPAA docs, pricing, and propose a benchmark plan. Recommend pilot: Hosted HIPAA-configured for low-friction early validation + Dedicated trial for BYOK and throughput validation. Next call — technical deep-dive week of 2026-09-21 with Marcus and Liam.
[07:17] Ethan Moore: Works for us.
[07:19] Sofia Ruiz: Thanks, please include DPA and SCCs.
[07:22] Ava Martinez: Will do, we'll follow up by Wednesday. Thanks everyone.
[07:25] Dr. Priya Kapoor: Thanks, bye.
[07:27] [call ends]
